facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He ended up doing three people's jobs after a client loss.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October. We lost a big client, half of the team got moved on to the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Workday habits are long
facts.content: Daniel stays at his desk answering messages late at night. He thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Sleep problems reported
facts.content: Daniel reports terrible sleep quality. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours. I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Waking up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and thinks about work. He calculates how little sleep he will get.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep. My head just starts. Shipping schedules, decline, weather and forgotten something. Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights. He runs until about five before getting up to make tea.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest. Then I'll run till about five and get up and make tea.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father is mostly himself but is slower and gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: He's slower. He gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Carer responsibilities are heavy
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. He manages neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto. All care for their father falls on Daniel.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto so all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Guilt about caregiving
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying he is tired when he is ill. He does not say anything to Hannah about it.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. She calls him every Sunday. She's not the one who's neglecting him. So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: Sister's contact with Daniel
facts.content: Hannah calls Daniel every Sunday. Hannah asks how Daniel is.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday. She asks how I am, Lise Freund.

facts.heading: GP tests normal
facts.content: Daniel's GP did blood tests which were all normal. The GP mentioned stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend expressed concern
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire said she was done watching Daniel disappear. Claire is patient and makes tea.
facts.evidence: She said she was done watching me disappear. She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire's physical changes
facts.content: Daniel noticed that Claire is wearing other hair.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's wearing other hair too.

facts.heading: Stopped going running
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. He had done it for six years.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. I've done it for six years.

facts.heading: Legs feel like lead
facts.content: Daniel's legs feel like lead after stopping running.
facts.evidence: My legs feel like lead.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He described running as the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Emails cause avoidance
facts.content: Emails are what stop Daniel from saying yes to things. He has to deal with 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. If I'm away, I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price.

facts.heading: Stopped running for reason
facts.content: Daniel stopped running because he could not face it.
facts.evidence: Because I can't face it.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: But he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answering emails is necessary
facts.content: Daniel answers emails every time, even when in bed, because he fears his boss will think he is not committed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Then he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: There is a restructuring in the spring, and Daniel is afraid they will let him go.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Feelings after potential job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would feel relieved but also horrible about being relieved if he were let go.
facts.evidence: I'd think part of me would be relieved and I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Feeling apart from tiredness
facts.content: Daniel feels flat and irritable apart from tiredness.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. His heart was going and his hands were shaking.
facts.evidence: I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. Heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Heart attack thought
facts.content: Daniel thought for a second that what he experienced was a heart attack, but it passed.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Previous frightening event
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening events a couple of times. One was on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: A couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fright means losing it
facts.content: Daniel's fright means he is losing it. He fears he will end up coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. I'm gonna end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day. He has started having wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day, and I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Wine consumption frequency
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine in the evenings. He finds it helps for an hour.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three. Easy. It works for an hour.

facts.heading: Sleep schedule irregularity
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning. He knows the wine is not helping him sleep.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Feeling about wine use
facts.content: Daniel feels the wine use is not useful. He feels like he is listing everything wrong with him.
facts.evidence: It doesn't feel useful. Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Carrying burdens
facts.content: Daniel thinks he has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time. He thinks the nights are what he carries.
facts.evidence: I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time. The nights, I think

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Grandfather's coping style
facts.content: Daniel observed his grandfather's way of handling things. The grandfather just got on with it.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there. Daniel thinks he is not weak.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak.

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after speaking. He notes that it is normal to feel shaky.
facts.evidence: Dired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Session scheduling next week
facts.content: The therapist asked if they could meet the same time next week. Daniel confirmed they will be there.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here.
